evidence.claim: Musk says SpaceX closed $40B of GPU debt on its investment-grade rating and Starlink and launch revenue, while lenders have nearly shut out AI data center firms without other revenue.
evidence.numbers: No lenders, rates or terms given; the FT-reported Apollo package was still described as under discussion on 20 October, so the close is unconfirmed (single source).

evidence.claim: Josh preview: Google backstops neocloud leases as credit derivatives, $43.8B notional at 30 June with an estimated $24.1B more agreed in principle; at TeraWulf and Cipher about $1.3B to $1.7B per site of 168 MW or more.
evidence.numbers: The backstop is what turns a neocloud lease into financeable cash flow; Google keeps step-in and termination rights.

evidence.claim: 3Q26 10-Q: data center financing 'has generally become more difficult'; neoclouds, colocation providers and other tenants are increasingly viewed as high credit risks, which may cancel projects and push developers to negotiate lower equipment prices.
evidence.numbers: A Brookfield-affiliated financing vehicle was 26% of 3Q revenue and the largest receivable (31%); the supplier is carrying more of the working capital (contract assets $858.6mn).

evidence.claim: Meta backs two off-balance-sheet JV campuses (Louisiana/Hyperion, Texas/El Paso) with 4-year initial leases plus residual value guarantees. Partners and their lenders fund 80%, and the leases and guarantees of an AA- tenant carry the debt.
evidence.numbers: Max RVG $41.49bn at 30 Sep 2026 vs $28.09bn at YE25; total max exposure $68.40bn; development cost ~$27bn and ~$14bn.

evidence.claim: A mature, listed cloud provider signed a 10-year, 20 MW colocation lease from Q2 2027 for more than $400M over the initial term.
evidence.numbers: About $2M per MW per year on the lower figure; the article headline says $700M and does not explain the gap. Small sites can sign listed-tenant paper.

evidence.claim: The tenant's own credit is drifting: Meta had negative free cash flow, moved to net debt, and created non-voting Class C stock for capital raising, among other purposes (also employee compensation, acquisitions, general corporate purposes). Management said it has no specific financing plans.
evidence.numbers: FCF -$2.12bn; cash and securities $82.45bn vs debt $83.67bn; capex $34.91bn = 106% of OCF.

evidence.claim: FT: Anthropic is offering Blackstone more than 10% on $9B of debt backed by Anthropic's five-year chip lease payments.
evidence.numbers: Even the largest lab's lease paper prices at double digits when it is not wrapped by an investment-grade parent. Reuters could not verify (single source).
evidence.source: The Star, citing Reuters and the FT

evidence.claim: JPMorgan and Goldman guaranteed only the $1.3B lease-backed term loan in Volta's $5.0B package; the $3.7B GPU term loan was sold best-efforts.
evidence.numbers: Both loans priced at about 11.2% to 11.75% yield to maturity, per PitchBook LCD data (single source).

evidence.claim: AMD agreed credit support for TensorWave's 222 MW lease at Fermi, a chip supplier standing behind a neocloud tenant.
Wells Fargo puts AWS- or Nvidia-backed data center bonds at about 6.8–7.2% and CoreWeave- or Oracle-backed at 8–9% or more.
Project debt backed by Google-supported and investment-grade leases priced at about 6.1–6.2%.
A facility backed by three-year contracts with weaker customers priced at SOFR + 550 bps and had to widen in syndication.
Phase II notes against an unbacked CoreWeave lease priced at 9.875%, the most expensive project debt among landlords.
Josh AMZN preview: Cipher's 70 MW Stingray lease is 15-year triple-net with a 3% escalator and an Amazon.com, Inc. guarantee of rent and opex; Amazon pays overruns above $10.5M per IT MW.
evidence.numbers: The parent guarantee let Cipher raise about $810M of project debt; Josh estimates about $128 to $159 per kW-month.

evidence.claim: A facility backed by one investment-grade customer priced at SOFR + 225 bps, rated A3.

question: Does the tenant's credit, not the asset, set what developers and neoclouds pay to borrow?
summary: Every 2026 financing points the same way. Debt backed by investment-grade contracts or a hyperscaler guarantee (Google backstops, Amazon's parent guarantee at Cipher) prices near 6-7%; GPU debt without that wrapper now pays 11% or more (Volta), and even Anthropic is reported paying above 10% on lease-backed chip debt. Musk's claim that only borrowers with non-AI revenue can still raise money fits the pattern, though his $40B close is unconfirmed. Status unchanged: this week added more evidence in the same direction.
title: Tenant credit sets the cost of capital
